time.original: Increase in dietary and mobility variation by about AD 700.
time.method: Published date convention retained; no new radiocarbon calibration. BCE uses astronomical year numbering (1 BCE = 0); calendar BP is referenced to 1950.
time.interpretation: The authors identify a shift around 700 CE in the variation among sampled individuals, within a much longer history of activity at the site.

claims.text: Cerro Juan Díaz's sampled individuals show wider diet and mobility variation after about 700 CE.

sources.title: La industria prehispánica de conchas marinas en Gran Coclé, Panamá
sources.venue: Universidad Complutense de Madrid doctoral dissertation
sources.access: Dissertation text includes a valid coordinate for the Operation 8 area. Published regional and site maps independently confirm the La Villa River setting.

review.summary: Over the long history of Cerro Juan Díaz, chemical signatures in bones and teeth record changing foods and movement. Around 700 CE, the diets and mobility histories of the people sampled began to vary more widely.
review.limitations: The results are from 49 sampled individuals. Isotopes reflect combinations of foods and local geology, which limit assignments of individual origins and ranks.
review.discussion: The village occupied land on both banks of the La Villa River near Parita Bay. Food waste includes freshwater and marine resources, while excavated areas preserve buildings, workshops and burials. The study found additional age- and sex-associated differences by 1150 CE. Operation 5 offers a separate record of burials over a former building floor during that later period.
review.provenance: The existing isotope observation is retained and updated using the open publisher article and separate excavations at the same place.
history: 2026-10-29: Original-source review with access and inference limits.
2026-11-17: Updated the site-area coordinate from published field documentation and linked later mortuary evidence.

claims.text: Taumako skeletal evidence includes healed trauma and a small number of piercing or sharp-force injuries relevant to interpersonal violence.
claims.explanation: The sample spans many burials, not one massacre or continuous warfare. Injury type does not identify an attacker, and healed injuries cannot be equated with homicide.
